value.rationale: Determining the exact largest cross-sectional volume of a natural finite Euclidean cylinder, and precisely when the maximizing plane tilts off the axis, is a fundamental and motivated section-extremum question. The strict dimension-dependent threshold, unique oblique angle, explicit four-dimensional closed maximum, and sharp onset quantify a geometric phase transition that is not implied by the predecessor's 3D theorem or unsolved general bounds. This is a complete natural classification with utility as a sharp analytic benchmark rather than a routine individual integral computation.
